prompt:
A crate of mass 140 kg rests on the flat horizontal floor of a freight elevator. The acceleration of free fall is 9.81 m s^-2.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Freight elevator cab carrying a crate of mass 140 kg on its floor. Upward cable tension and vertical downward gravitational pull are indicated.]
(a) The elevator accelerates vertically upwards from rest to a speed of 3.60 m s^-1 in a time interval of 2.40 s. Calculate the acceleration of the elevator. [2]
(b) Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force exerted by the elevator floor on the crate during this upward acceleration. [2]
(c) The elevator reaches the top floor and comes to rest. If the elevator cable were to sever so that the elevator fell freely under gravity, state the magnitude of the normal contact force on the crate and explain your answer. [2]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the acceleration of the elevator.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the normal contact force exerted by the elevator floor on the crate during this upward acceleration.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State the magnitude of the normal contact force on the crate during free fall and explain your answer.

part_enrichment.guidance: Use uniform acceleration equation a = Delta v / Delta t.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Inverting time and velocity or using incorrect initial velocity.

part_enrichment.guidance: Sum upward forces: R - mg = ma, so R = m(g + a).
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Calculating only the net force ma (210 N) or subtracting ma from weight.

marking_points.criterion: Both the elevator and the crate accelerate downwards at g (free fall), so no contact force is required between floor and crate (R = m(g - g) = 0).

part_enrichment.guidance: Explain apparent weightlessness: floor and crate accelerate at g simultaneously.
part_enrichment.common_pitfall: Claiming gravity becomes zero instead of the contact force.

hints: In (a), use definition of acceleration a = (v - u) / t.
In (b), set up Newton's second law vertically: R - mg = ma.
In (c), in free fall both elevator and crate accelerate downwards at g.
solution:
(a) a = (3.60 - 0) / 2.40 = 1.50 m s^-2.
(b) R = m(g + a) = 140 * (9.81 + 1.50) = 140 * 11.31 = 1583 N = 1580 N.
(c) Contact force = 0 N. In free fall, both the elevator floor and the crate accelerate downwards at g, so the floor does not exert any contact force on the crate.
teacher_walkthrough: In part (a), determine acceleration from kinematics: a = Delta v / Delta t = 3.60 / 2.40 = 1.50 m s^-2.
In part (b), write vertical equation of motion: R - mg = ma => R = m(g + a) = 140 * 11.31 = 1583.4 N = 1580 N.
In part (c), state that contact force drops to 0 N (B1) because both crate and elevator accelerate downwards at g together (B1).
